newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: PRESS DIGEST - South Korean newspapers - June 25.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - South Korean newspapers - June 25.

text.p: The following is a summary of major stories in leading South Korean newspapers, prepared by Reuters in Seoul. Reuters has not checked the stories and does not guarantee their accuracy.
- The government will maintain the current 4 percent individual shareholding limit in banks in order to prevent chaebol domination of the financial sector.
- Korea has decided to file complaints against the U.S. and Canada with the World Trade Organization next month, with respect to their anti-dumping regulation on Korean export goods.
- The opposition United Liberal Democrats on Tuesday nominated its leader, Kim Jong-pil, as the party's candidate for the presidential election in December.

- President Kim Young-sam, in a keynote speech before the U.N. General Assembly Monday, proposed that South and North Korea joinly preserve the inter-Korean border area, which has been deserted since the end of the Korean War in 1953.
- In the past year or so, as many as 80 Korean banks, insurers, leasing firms and merchant banks have opened branches in Hong Kong.
